title: Priming spike runbook and standup notes
content:
Summary:
This note captures the priming-related latency spike we observed on canary on 2026-11-17, the experiments we ran during the 11/18 perf sync, and the short runbook to reproduce and mitigate. Primary hypothesis: a change in kernel selection triggered by PR #8143 interacts poorly with our prefix/KV cache eviction heuristics for short-sequence requests (seq_len <= 64), causing a cascade of slower attention kernels and elevated p95/p99.

Attendees:
- Priya Menon (owner)
- Evan Liu
- Marissa Koh
- Jonah Patel
- Ava Rodriguez
- On-call: Marco Silva (SRE, async)

Observed symptom (canary):
- Date/time window: 2026-11-17 03:20 – 03:50 UTC
- Workload: production-simulated shadow load, majority small seq requests (prompt ~20–40 tokens, generation limited to 24 tokens).
- Baseline before regress: p50 ~ 38ms, p95 ~ 120ms, p99 ~ 210ms for small-seq path.
- During spike: p50 ~ 55ms, p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 890ms. Throughput dropped ~18% at same offered QPS.
- Memory/CPU/GPU: GPU utilization unchanged; modest bump in host CPU sys time on the inference sidecar; no OOMs.
- Correlation: spike aligns with canary fleet rolling to serving-runtime:v2.14.6 (kernel selector change).

Repro instructions (quick):
1) Checkout the canary build: git checkout refs/pull/8143/head && bazel build //serving:runtime_canary
2) Run bench harness in local infra (use the small-seq profile):
   export MODEL=gpt-small-q8
   export BENCH_SEQ=48
   export BATCH=8
   ./tools/jbench --model $MODEL --seq $BENCH_SEQ --batch $BATCH --warmup 120 --duration 300 --profile > jbench_smallseq_canary.log
3) Capture kernel selection traces: set SERVING_TRACE=kernel_selection:true,kvcache:state
   ./tools/jbench --env SERVING_TRACE=... --model ...
4) Compare against stable runtime (v2.14.5) under identical load.

What we ran in sync (11/18):
- Shadow run A: v2.14.6 vs v2.14.5 side-by-side, 30 minute runs, 1k RPS offered (small-seq focussed).
- Kernel trace extract: grep kernel_selection jbench_smallseq_canary.log | awk '{print $6,$8}' > kernel_choices.txt
- KV cache walk: instrumented run with kv_probe enabled (10% sample).

Key findings from traces:
- v2.14.6 changes: more aggressive fused-attention path chosen when seq < 128 if tensor layout meets criteria. In many small-seq samples we saw selection flip between 'fused-attn-v2' and 'matmul-stream-v1' mid-request due to on-device shape rounding after quantization fallback.
- When flip occurs, we observed an extra kernel swap and a temporary stall while CUDA kernels rebind (~150–350ms on average for affected requests). This explains the p95/p99 jump.
- KV cache eviction: our prefix cache TTL/temperature heuristic sometimes triggered eviction during warmup combined with the kernel flip; when eviction happened, subsequent requests paid the cost of re-prime + kernel swap.
- The problem is amplified for low-latency small-seq customers (dedicated and hosted light endpoints). High-seq steady workloads less impacted.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel selector bug in v2.14.6 that flips selection when encountering quantization rounding — likely root cause.
2) KV cache heuristic aggressiveness surfaces the kernel flip more often (secondary amplifier).
3) Host-side scheduling causing delay during kernel rebind (less likely given GPU traces).

Immediate mitigations tested during sync: (results)
- Rollback canary to v2.14.5: p95/p99 returned to baseline in 10 minutes. (Confirmed)
- Pin kernel selector to stable on canary builds via env override KERNEL_PREF=stable_fused (experiment): reduced flip rate by ~92%, p95 improved but not fully baseline (because some code paths still falling back).
- Increased prefix cache temperature threshold (temporary +30%): reduced eviction events by ~60% and lowered repeat prime cost.

Short runbook (for on-call and perf leads):
1) If small-seq p95 > 350ms on canary, revert rollout to previous runtime tag (v2.14.5) and notify perf channel.
2) Apply KERNEL_PREF=stable_fused override to the canary deployment while debugging continues.
3) Temporarily bump prefix cache temperature threshold for affected shards: curl -X PATCH $OPS_API/shards/{id}/cache?temp_mult=1.3
4) Collect traces: jbench profile logs + kvcache sample + nsys GPU profile from 10 affected requests.
5) Open a bisect PR if we identify specific commit (assign to Evan/Liang).

Action items (owners & dates):
- Evan Liu: prepare kernel-selector unit tests + minimal reproducer (due 2026-11-21).
- Marissa Koh: run full fleet shadow run with KERNEL_PREF override and report p95/p99 across regions (due 2026-11-20).
- Jonah Patel: add telemetry to kvcache to emit "priming-miss-with-kernelflip" event (due 2026-11-22).
- Ava Rodriguez: coordinate canary rollback and verify rollback runbook; update incident postmortem stub in Confluence (due 2026-11-19).
- Priya Menon: triage linked PR #8143 and assign kernel author for follow-up; own coordination with SRE (ongoing).

Longer-term follow-ups (not blocking rollback):
- Add a conservative debounce window in kernel selector to avoid mid-request flips; consider pinning per-request kernel once chosen until next request.
- Revisit kvcache eviction heuristics for small-seq heavy endpoints; consider sticky priming for first N requests.
- Add continuous test that runs small-seq shadow runs during any kernel selector change PR gating.

Notes / discussion highlights from sync:
- Marco (SRE): recommended automating rollback path in deployment pipeline so we can revert a rollout rapidly without manual patch.
- Evan: kernel flip repro is non-deterministic but we found a 1-in-250 trigger when running 10k small-seq requests with the canary tag. We should add a fuzz harness to increase coverage.
- Marissa: customer-facing risk low for now (mostly canary), but dedicated customers with low-latency SLAs could be impacted if rollout continues.

Appendix — quick commands used during the session:
- Side-by-side bench (canary + stable):
  ./tools/jbench --model gpt-small-q8 --seq 48 --batch 8 --warmup 120 --duration 180 --tag canary > canary.log &
  ./tools/jbench --model gpt-small-q8 --seq 48 --batch 8 --warmup 120 --duration 180 --tag stable > stable.log &
- Kernel trace extraction:
  grep kernel_selection canary.log | cut -d' ' -f4- > canary_kernel_choices.txt
- Quick kv sample probe (10%):
  export KV_PROBE_SAMPLE=0.1 && ./tools/jbench --model ... --profile

If you’re taking an action from the list, drop a short update in #serving-runtime-perf (thread: 1721234567.000123) when you start and when you finish so we can coordinate rollback and customer comms.

End.
